episode.title: Allow keyless cloud authentication without changing the configured principal
episode.before: At parent c2d63fbe582a3d37051816dea4775687a4ab9896, both the CLI authentication preflight and core model validation rejected the selected cloud-hosted auth mode whenever no API key resolved. Supplying a placeholder key was unsafe because the SDK interpreted any key as an alternate express authentication mode. Client construction also depended on an environment-variable side effect to select the cloud endpoint, so startup paths that skipped that side effect could target the wrong endpoint.
episode.after: At fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430, a nonblank project configuration permits the keyless default-credential path only when the selected provider entry does not declare its own key variable. Core client construction derives cloud mode directly from the selected auth type and leaves the API key absent. Missing-credential messages describe the keyless alternative only where applicable, while status preflight reports the unverified default-credential state as unknown rather than claiming a token exists.
episode.diff: The change adds a shared, whitespace-aware project predicate; makes CLI and core credential gates accept eligible project-only configurations; preserves declared key-variable authority; explicitly selects cloud SDK mode from the auth type; keeps absent keys undefined; adds conditional default-credential guidance to errors; and represents keyless preflight status as indeterminate. Tests cover eligible and excluded configurations, missing project behavior, whitespace, strict validation, endpoint-mode construction, key absence, and preflight status.

evidence_units.claim: Commit fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430 identifies the prior failure: cloud authentication required an API key, while passing a placeholder key switched the SDK to an incompatible express mode; it states that project-only configuration should allow the SDK to resolve default credentials.

In the parent, CLI validation unconditionally called the API-key error resolver for the cloud auth type and rejected missing keys; the change first checks whether the selected model entry is eligible for default credentials and whether a nonblank project is configured.

The CLI eligibility check resolves the selected model-provider entry and excludes entries declaring envKey, preventing an unset declared secret from silently falling through to another principal. Project lookup considers process.env first and settings.env second.

Core introduces one project-configured predicate that trims the configured value, and its default-credential eligibility predicate requires the cloud auth type, no explicit apiKeyEnvKey, and a configured project.

Core model validation changes from rejecting every configuration without apiKey to accepting a missing key only when the default-credential eligibility predicate succeeds; explicit apiKeyEnvKey is forwarded to error construction.

SDK client construction maps the selected cloud auth type to vertexai=true when no explicit vertexai option overrides it and converts an empty API key to undefined, allowing SDK-side default credential resolution without relying on a prior environment side effect.

The CLI authentication entry point applies eligibility and project checks before session startup, while core validation independently applies the same keyless contract to resolved model configurations.

Missing-credential errors append the project/default-credential hint only for the cloud auth type when no explicit key variable was declared, avoiding unusable advice for other auth types and key-bound entries.

ACP preflight recognizes an eligible project-only configuration but reports status and hasToken as unknown because project routing configuration does not prove that a usable default credential resolves.

CLI tests specify acceptance for project-only environment and provider configurations, rejection when neither key nor project exists, preservation of an entry's declared envKey, and rejection of whitespace-only project values.

Core tests specify successful normal and strict validation for an eligible project-only configuration, rejection without a project, exclusion of other auth types, preservation of explicit key-variable requirements, and inclusion or suppression of the project hint according to eligibility.
evidence_units.source: fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430:packages/core/src/core/contentGenerator.test.ts; Vertex AI Application Default Credentials suite

evidence_units.claim: A client-construction test specifies that selecting the cloud auth type produces vertexai=true and apiKey=undefined even when the mode-selection environment variable is unset.
evidence_units.source: fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430:packages/core/src/core/contentGenerator.test.ts; builds the client in Vertex mode from the auth type alone

evidence_units.claim: An ACP test specifies that a project-only keyless configuration yields auth status unknown, hasToken unknown, and no error kind rather than a confirmed credential.

Documentation states that project-only authentication requires explicit selection of the cloud auth type, that every API-key source must remain absent, and that entries declaring envKey do not fall back to default credentials.

The pinned commit contains focused automated test additions across CLI validation, core validation/client construction, and ACP preflight, but the supplied checkout has its tracked worktree files staged as deleted, so these tests were inspected from Git objects rather than executed in this extraction.

candidate_atomics.name: classify_keyless_credential_eligibility
candidate_atomics.title: Classify whether a keyless credential path is eligible
candidate_atomics.description: Determine whether the selected authentication mode may use ambient default credentials without overriding a provider entry that explicitly declares a key source.

semantic_action.intent: Permit an ambient credential resolver only when routing context is present and no explicit secret contract would be bypassed.
semantic_action.pre_state: A selected provider configuration has no resolved API key and may or may not declare its own key variable or contain a usable project identifier.
semantic_action.post_state: The configuration is classified as keyless-eligible only for the supported auth mode, with no declared key variable and a nonblank project identifier.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise project-present, project-absent, whitespace-only, alternate-auth-type, and explicit-key-variable cases; only the eligible project-only cases may pass.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile_authentication_gates
candidate_atomics.title: Apply one credential contract across startup validators
candidate_atomics.description: Make CLI preflight and core configuration validation accept the same eligible project-only state while retaining errors for all excluded states.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent an authentication method accepted at one startup boundary from being rejected at another.
semantic_action.pre_state: Multiple startup gates independently treat absence of an API key as a credential failure.
semantic_action.post_state: Each gate accepts a missing key only under the shared keyless eligibility contract and continues to reject missing credentials otherwise.
semantic_action.validation: Run focused CLI and core validation cases for eligible keyless configuration, missing project, strict validation, explicit key-variable configuration, and unrelated auth modes.

candidate_atomics.name: construct_client_for_selected_auth_mode
candidate_atomics.title: Construct the SDK client for the selected authentication mode
candidate_atomics.description: Select the cloud endpoint directly from the resolved auth type and preserve an absent API key so the SDK can resolve ambient credentials.

semantic_action.intent: Route requests to the intended cloud endpoint without converting a keyless configuration into a conflicting key-based mode.
semantic_action.pre_state: Client construction may depend on an earlier environment mutation, and a placeholder or empty key can alter SDK authentication semantics.
semantic_action.post_state: The selected cloud auth type produces explicit cloud mode with no API key supplied; other auth types retain SDK environment fallback unless explicitly configured.
semantic_action.validation: Construct the client with the cloud auth type, a configured project, no mode-selection environment value, and no API key; assert cloud mode is true and the key is undefined.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve_explicit_credential_authority
candidate_atomics.title: Preserve explicitly declared credential authority
candidate_atomics.description: Keep a declared secret source mandatory instead of silently authenticating through ambient credentials when that secret is missing.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid silently changing the authenticated principal after a configured secret fails to resolve.
semantic_action.pre_state: A provider entry declares a key variable, the variable is unset, and ambient credentials might otherwise be available.
semantic_action.post_state: Validation continues to fail on the declared key variable and does not offer or activate the ambient credential path.
semantic_action.validation: Configure a declared key variable plus a project while leaving the variable unset; assert validation fails on that variable in both CLI and core and omits the keyless hint.

candidate_atomics.name: report_unverified_ambient_credentials
candidate_atomics.title: Report ambient credentials as unverified until session startup
candidate_atomics.description: Represent routing readiness separately from proof that an ambient credential can actually resolve.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid presenting project configuration as proof of a usable authentication token.
semantic_action.pre_state: No API key is observed, but the configuration is eligible to attempt ambient credential resolution at session start.
semantic_action.post_state: Preflight reports an indeterminate authentication state with no confirmed token and defers credential proof to session startup.
semantic_action.validation: Request preflight status for an eligible keyless configuration and assert unknown status, unknown token presence, and no immediate missing-key error.

candidate_atomics.name: emit_applicable_credential_recovery_guidance
candidate_atomics.title: Emit recovery guidance only for applicable credential paths
candidate_atomics.description: Tell users about ambient credentials when that path can work, while retaining precise key-source errors for excluded configurations.

semantic_action.intent: Direct users toward a valid recovery path without encouraging placeholder credentials or impossible fallbacks.
semantic_action.pre_state: Credential validation fails and the error formatter knows the auth type and whether a key variable was explicitly declared.
semantic_action.post_state: Eligible keyless configurations mention the project-based alternative; unrelated auth types and explicit-key-variable entries do not.
semantic_action.validation: Assert project guidance appears for eligible missing-credential errors in normal and strict modes and is absent for unrelated auth types and explicit-key-variable entries.

candidate_workflows.name: enable_safe_ambient_credential_resolution
candidate_workflows.title: Enable ambient credentials without weakening credential precedence
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution chain for adding a keyless ambient authentication path across validation, client construction, diagnostics, and status reporting while preventing silent principal changes.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow a supported provider mode to resolve ambient default credentials from a project-scoped configuration while preserving explicit secret precedence, correct endpoint routing, truthful status, and actionable failures.
when_to_use: A provider SDK supports ambient or application-default credentials, but application validation currently requires an explicit API key.
Passing a placeholder credential changes SDK mode or disables the intended ambient credential resolver.
The same authentication decision is enforced at multiple startup or configuration boundaries.
anti_goals: Do not fabricate, inject, or pass a placeholder API key to satisfy validation.
Do not silently fall back to ambient credentials when the selected provider entry declares a specific key source.
Do not infer the selected authentication mode from project configuration alone when explicit mode selection is required.
Do not report a configured project as proof that a usable credential has resolved.
Do not broaden the keyless path to unrelated authentication modes.
not_applicable_when: The provider SDK does not support ambient credential resolution.
No routing context required by the ambient resolver is configured.
The selected provider entry explicitly requires a key source that must remain authoritative.
The authentication mode cannot be selected independently of credential presence.
inputs: resolved API key and its source
project or routing identifier from process and settings
startup validation and preflight entry points
workflow_graph.entry_state: The intended provider mode is selected and ambient credentials may exist, but missing-key checks prevent startup or a placeholder key changes SDK behavior; validation, construction, and status surfaces may disagree.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Eligible project-only configurations pass every startup validation gate, construct the SDK client in the intended mode with no key, preserve explicit secret contracts, provide applicable recovery guidance, and leave actual ambient credential resolution unconfirmed until session startup.

steps.condition: Always establish the exact boundary before relaxing any missing-key check.
steps.validation: Boundary tests distinguish nonblank routing context from blank or whitespace values and exclude unrelated auth modes and declared key sources.

steps.condition: Apply whenever configurations may declare their own credential source.
steps.validation: An unset declared key remains an error even when ambient routing context is present.

steps.condition: Apply to every gate that can reject the resolved authentication configuration before client use.
steps.validation: CLI and core validators agree on eligible, ineligible, strict, and explicit-key configurations.

steps.condition: Apply when the SDK's endpoint or authentication behavior depends on mode flags or key presence.
steps.validation: The constructed client receives the intended mode flag and no API key without relying on a prior environment mutation.

steps.condition: Apply to missing-credential errors exposed by the affected validation gates.
steps.validation: The ambient-credential hint appears only where the classifier says the path is applicable.

steps.condition: Apply when a preflight or status surface reports token availability before the SDK attempts ambient resolution.
steps.validation: Eligible project-only status is indeterminate rather than authenticated or missing-key failed.

validation_ladder: Predicate-level cases: nonblank, absent, and whitespace-only routing identifiers.
Precedence cases: declared key source remains mandatory despite available ambient context.
Cross-gate cases: CLI and core validators accept and reject the same configurations, including strict mode.
Construction case: selected mode reaches the SDK explicitly and the key remains undefined.
Diagnostic cases: recovery guidance is present only for eligible failures.
Status case: routing readiness is reported as unknown credential availability.
Runtime follow-up: start a session in an environment with valid ambient credentials and separately verify failure with unavailable ambient credentials.
stop_conditions: Stop if project or routing configuration cannot be distinguished from proof of credential availability.
Stop if a declared credential source would be bypassed or the authenticated principal could change silently.
Stop if any startup validator still rejects an otherwise eligible configuration.
Stop if client construction sends any placeholder key or selects the wrong endpoint mode.
Stop if tests cannot demonstrate exclusion of unrelated auth types and explicit-key configurations.
unresolved_or_deferred: Actual external default-credential resolution is delegated to the provider SDK and is not proven by the unit tests in the pinned change.
Focused tests were not executed during extraction because the supplied checkout's tracked worktree files are staged as deleted; test contracts were inspected directly from the pinned Git objects.
GitHub issue body, PR discussion, reviews, and status-check results are unavailable in the evidence bundle.

unresolved_questions: Were the focused CLI, core, and ACP tests executed successfully in CI for PR 9017? The bundle does not include status checks, and the supplied worktree state prevented local execution without altering user-owned staged deletions.

Does a live session successfully resolve valid ambient credentials and surface provider SDK failures appropriately when ambient credentials are unavailable? The pinned tests mock client construction and do not provide an external authentication oracle.
